gmm.support: very strong support for two groups
gmm.verdict: ΔBIC = +1227.1 (one group 33197.0, two groups 31969.9): very strong support for two groups. BIC compares Gaussian shapes, and a single skewed cloud can earn two components, so this is evidence, not proof. But its two groups are barely the DS / IED split (adjusted Rand 0.05, where 1 is the same split and 0 is chance; 61% of events the same): two Gaussians fit the cloud's SHAPE better than one, which a single skewed spectrum also does. Read the split-axis histogram before reading this as two populations.

dbic_scale: very strong support for two groups

rule: Pooled over 22 recordings from 22 mice, in pooled raw units: the cluster whose centre has more 500–1000 Hz power is called IED: +17.5 dB against +9.3 dB for the other, which is called DS (2272 DS, 1732 IED, 1 not measured; 39 assigned on 2 of 3 axes (half-width unresolved even at 50 ms)).

scale.why: Pooled raw units, z-scored once across the pool: differences in size between mice stay visible, impedance and placement included.

split_axis.unit: z, 0 at the midpoint, DS negative
